traps.note: Repro example names the surface: a bytes value through dumps with reject_bytes=False and a bad continuation byte.
Truncation is covered only by the general 'not a complete encoding of exactly one code point' rule; no end-of-buffer or truncation wording.
Object keys are never mentioned; covered only by 'every byte sequence it accepts' in the writing property.
Out-of-range sequences fall under the general 'exactly one code point' rule; no code-point-maximum or 4-byte-arm wording.

traps.quote: When the library reads data from JSON text, a byte sequence in the text that is not a complete encoding of exactly one code point must likewise be refused
traps.note: A separate Reading section widens the property to the decoder, which a dumps-only one-bug version would not need.

traps.quote: When the library reads data from JSON text, a byte sequence in the text that is not a complete encoding of exactly one code point must likewise be refused
